mainTitle: Natural Language Processing (NLP) Sentiment Analysis of the book Odyssey by written by Homer
category: Natural Language Processing / Sentiment Analysis / Digital Humanities
description:
The project used a supervised ML combining FastText word embeddings. Sentence embeddings and sentiment features were used to train the model, with an 80/20 train-test.

Additionally, three dictionaries were used to normalize character names, epithets, assign weights to actions and determine whether relationships represent help, obstruction, or neutrality, and a final dictionary to resolve personal pronouns to the corresponding character entities.

As a result it was possible to get  plots of sentiment interactions per chapter.

graphs.text:
Sentences were identified using the model en_core_web_sm forsegmentation, which detects boundaries based on punctuation, syntax, and context. TTR was then calculated for each sentence as the number of unique words divided by the total number of words.

There is a large peak around TTR ≈ 1.0. In many sentences, no word is repeated within the same sentence. At the sentence level, there is almost no lexical repetition, as expected given the high diversity typical of a book.

shortTitle: Deep Learning CNN for Cell Morphology
mainTitle: Deep Learning for Biological Cell Morphology Analysis
category: Deep Learning / Biomedical AI / Computer Vision / Image Processing
description: This project of deep learning project for images in biological cells after exposure to different compounds. Using different CNN  models, the project explores how cellular features can help predict compoung effects throught morfology. The images are provided by the Broad Institute, a biomedical research organization that collaborates with MIT and Harvard.
modelInterpretation:
This model of deep learning approach to classify the Mechanism of Action (MOA) of  compounds from biological cell images.The images contains fluorescence microscopy images of cells treated with different compounds and concentrations.

The project  includes data exploration, preprocessing, image normalization, train-validation-test partitioning, class encoding, data augmentation, class balancing, use in differtents convolutional neural networks (CNN) models with different droputs, batch sizes and others hyperparameters.

Sensitivity analyses were also performed to assess the impact of visual effects that can be also in the microsopy such as rotation, zoom, contrast, and Gaussian noise.

mainTitle: Hybrid LSTM-CNN Model for Tesla Stock Market Prediction
category: Deep Learning / Time Series / Financial Analytics / CNN / LSTM / Technical Indicators / Deep Learning
description: This project predicts the next-day direction of Tesla (TSLA) stock using deep learning. Historical stock price data are transformed into time sequences, and the target is used predict if next day the price increse or decrease using a hybrid model combining combining LSTM and CNN.
modelInterpretation:
The project compares Simple LSTM architecture and hybrid models combining  CNN and LSTM models.

Technical indicators were used such as RSI, MACD, ATR, and EMA. with  different time windows were implemented as 5,10 and 20 days to compare the performance. Overall accuracy remains close to 0.50–0.54, suggesting limited predictive power for next-day TSLA direction.  However the release a prediction app was done as a part of the project.
